title: Paper Reef Pharmacy — inference field jot
content:
TL;DR:
Quick capture from 11/05 sync with Paper Reef (small regional pharmacy chain). They want an embedded assistant for pharmacist triage + refill routing. Must be on a Private deployment (VPC) due to PHI-ish content, target p99 latency <300ms for short prompts, expected peak 60 reqs/s during 7–9am window for first pilot store set (10 stores), scale plan later.

Participants on call:
- Samir Patel (Paper Reef, Head of Platform)
- Dr. Elena Ortiz (Clinical lead)
- Abby Nguyen (Product manager)
- Ava Chen (Redwood SE) — owner
- Jordan Patel (Redwood) — notes

Background/context:
- Use case: pharmacist-facing assistant to summarize patient history, surface medication interactions, and propose refill options. Not customer-facing.
- Data flow: Paper Reef will push medication records + prescriptions via SFTP nightly; realtime queries hit a secure internal API that returns a patient record reference (no raw PHI in prompts ideally).
- Compliance: Must stay inside their VPC. They have SOC2 + regional privacy policy; plan: Private (VPC) deployment with KMS and audit logging.

Non-functional/requirements captured:
- Latency SLO: p95 <180ms, p99 <300ms for short retrieval+prompt combination.
- Throughput: baseline 5–10 rps, peak 60 rps (10 stores) during morning rush; expected growth to 500 rps in 6–9 months for full rollout (planning).
- Cost sensitivity: high — they want guidance on batching / quantization to bring down token cost for long summaries.
- Data residency: US-East only for pilot.
- Access controls: support for IdP (SAML/OIDC) and per-user RBAC; need audit trail for prompts and model outputs.
- Offline/on-prem option: they asked about an air-gapped future state but not required for pilot.

Architecture notes / suggestions (SE brain dump):
- Private deployment (VPC) with connector to their internal API (patient lookup). Avoid sending raw PHI to the model — use tokenized references + local verification layer that expands tokens post-hoc if needed.
- Suggest model family: mid-sized open encoder-decoder optimized for safety (we have Redwood-verified rM3-median / rM3-compact profile). For pilot pick a 13–25B variant with 8-bit quantization (fp16 -> int8/4 where supported) to balance latency and cost.
- KV cache: enable prefix cache for common prompts (triage template) and patient-stable sections (allergy list) to reduce repeated decode.
- Batching: conservative batching window 5–10ms to not blow latency SLO; adaptive batching during off-peak.
- Fallback policy: if model slower or lack capacity, fall back to a lightweight retrieval-only response (pre-canned bullet points) — they liked this idea.

Prompt / data handling gotchas (call notes):
- They will initially include short patient notes as plain text in the request; legal insisted on only sending pointers to full records. We need to confirm minimal safe prompt shape.
- Drug interaction rules must be auditable — need deterministic path where we can surface source citations (link to local drug DB). Model output must include the rule ID + confidence.
- Token limits: some patient histories exceed 8k tokens when expanded; discuss long-context strategies (summarize-on-write vs. retrieve-on-read).

Operational telemetry & observability (requested):
- Token-level cost logging per route + per-user (for billing).
- Latency breakdown (network + model + retrieval).
- Model output drift alerts tied to prompt test set (weekly evals).
- Audit log retention 1 year for pilot, exportable for compliance.

Open questions (to chase):
- Legal: confirm exact PHI elements allowed in transit. Action: Abby to send legal excerpt (due 11/08).
- Traffic profile: need hourly distribution for 14-day period. Action: Samir to provide CSV (JIRA PRJ-412).
- IdP integration details (SAML metadata). Action: Samir/Abby to share SAML metadata (secure link).
- Drug DB integration: which vendor? local mapping shape (fields). Action: Dr. Ortiz to share sample extract (anonymized).

Prompts / quick examples (work-in-progress):
- "Summarize the past 6 months of med history for patient_ref_23. Focus on meds, allergies, and interactions. Cite drug-db rule IDs. Output: 3 bullets + confidence score"
- "Given patient_ref_23 and new_prescription X, list top 3 interaction concerns and recommended pharmacist action (accept/reject/refer)."

Risks / gotchas we flagged:
- Sending raw PHI into hosted models — must enforce VPC for pilot.
- Overly aggressive batching could violate p99 latency during morning spike.
- Long-history documents -> model hallucination risk; need retrieval + verifiable citations.
- They will want deterministic responses for certain regulatory steps — model nondeterminism must be mitigated (temperature=0, template output).

Immediate next steps / action items:
- Abby: share legal excerpt on PHI transmission rules (due 2024-11-08).
- Samir: upload 14-day traffic CSV to JIRA ticket PRJ-412 (due 2024-11-10).
- Dr. Ortiz: anonymized drug DB sample and mapping (due 2024-11-12).
- Ava: draft pilot architecture diagram + cost estimate (initial) and post to Confluence (by 2024-11-12).
- Jordan: stub a prompt test suite (5 canonical prompts + expected outputs) and link to PRJ-412 (by 2024-11-13).

Notes to self (SE):
- Consider offering an initial 'safety wrapper' microservice that performs rules check (deterministic) before/after model call so Paper Reef has an auditable control plane.
- Precompute patient summary on nightly ingest (summarize-on-write) to reduce realtime token consumption; keep windowed incremental updates.
- Prepare two model profile options for the pilot: (A) higher perf 13B quantized (lower latency, moderate cost), (B) 25B more conservative outputs (better clinical phrasing) — show tradeoffs in cost sheet.

Conversation tone: pragmatic, cautious on PHI, eager to avoid surprises. They responded well to fallback/rescue approach.

---
Scratchpad ends — keep incremental edits here. Will move to shared Confluence once we have legal excerpt + traffic CSV.
